questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.question: The radius of gyration of a body about an axis is defined as the distance from the axis at which:
options: Its whole mass may be assumed concentrated to give the same moment of inertia
questions.explanation: I = Mk², so k depends on how the mass is distributed about the axis and not just on where the centre of mass is.
questions.ncertReference: Physics Class 11, Chapter 6: System of Particles and Rotational Motion

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: For a solid, the coefficients of linear, superficial and cubical expansion are related as:
questions.explanation: Area involves two dimensions and volume three, so β = 2α and γ = 3α, which is why expansion joints matter most for long structures.
questions.ncertReference: Physics Class 11, Chapter 10: Thermal Properties of Matter

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The electric potential at a distance r from an isolated point charge q in vacuum is:
questions.explanation: Potential is a scalar and varies as 1/r, while the field is a vector varying as 1/r². The first option is the magnitude of the field, not the potential.
questions.ncertReference: Physics Class 12, Chapter 2: Electrostatic Potential and Capacitance

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The standard enthalpy of formation of oxygen gas, O₂(g), at 298 K is:
options: Equal to its bond dissociation enthalpy
questions.explanation: An element in its most stable form under standard conditions is taken as the reference point, so its enthalpy of formation is defined as zero.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In a multistep reaction, the overall rate of the reaction is governed by:
options: The slowest, that is the rate determining step
questions.explanation: A reaction can go no faster than its slowest step, just as a queue moves at the pace of its slowest counter, and this is why order often differs from stoichiometry.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Fehling's solution is reduced to a reddish brown precipitate of cuprous oxide by:
questions.explanation: Aliphatic aldehydes give a positive test, ketones give none, and aromatic aldehydes such as benzaldehyde do not respond to Fehling's solution.
questions.ncertReference: Chemistry Class 12, Chapter 8: Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: Cytokinesis in a plant cell differs from that in an animal cell because in the plant cell:
options: A cleavage furrow pinches the cell in two
A cell plate forms from the centre outwards
questions.explanation: A rigid cell wall rules out furrowing, so vesicles fuse at the equator to build a cell plate that grows outwards into the middle lamella.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 11, Chapter 10: Cell Cycle and Cell Division

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: The first clinical gene therapy was given in 1990 to a girl suffering from a deficiency of the enzyme:
questions.explanation: ADA deficiency cripples immunity. Lymphocytes carrying a functional ADA gene were returned to the patient, but since they are not immortal the treatment had to be repeated.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 12, Chapter 10: Biotechnology and its Applications

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: Emphysema, in which the alveolar walls are damaged and the respiratory surface is reduced, is most often caused by:
questions.explanation: Chronic smoking destroys alveolar septa, so gas exchange area falls. Silicosis comes from stone dust, and pollen allergy causes asthma.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 11, Chapter 14: Breathing and Exchange of Gases

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: Aldosterone, secreted by the adrenal cortex, acts mainly on the kidney to:
options: Increase the reabsorption of sodium and water
Increase the loss of sodium in urine
questions.explanation: Aldosterone is a mineralocorticoid that conserves Na⁺ and water while promoting K⁺ loss, so it helps maintain blood volume and pressure.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 11, Chapter 19: Chemical Coordination and Integration
